summary.headline: Aster Q4 FY26 revenue rose 18% to INR 1,182 crore and operating EBITDA 26% to INR 244 crore, with the QCIL merger awaiting NCLT approval.
summary.overview: Aster's Q4 FY26 revenue from operations grew 18% YoY to INR 1,182 crore, driven by a 15% rise in patient volumes and a 9% rise in ARPP IP, with Kasargod still ramping up. Operating EBITDA rose 26% to INR 244 crore at a 20.7% margin, and excluding Kasargod the margin was 21.7%. Core hospitals and clinics posted 32% EBITDA growth at a 23.1% margin, and labs turned sharply profitable. The Quality Care (QCIL) merger has shareholder and creditor approval and awaits NCLT order, which management expects this quarter. Management presented combined proforma figures alongside Aster's standalone numbers.

financial_highlights.metric: Aster India operating EBITDA excl. Kasargod (FY26)
Combined proforma revenue (Aster + QCIL, Q4 FY26)

financial_highlights.change: from 7.6% in FY25 and -7.6% in FY24

segments.name: Kerala cluster
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR 604 crore, +21% YoY (+18% excl. Kasargod to INR 587 crore); EBITDA margin excl. Kasargod 25.6%, up 330 bps. MVT revenue up 51% YoY; inpatient volumes +11%.

segments.name: Karnataka & Maharashtra cluster
segments.commentary: Q4 revenue INR 394 crore, +11% YoY; ARPP IP +21%, IP volumes +3% after exit of low-yield government schemes at Aster Aadhar. EBITDA +25%, margin 24.5% (+260 bps).

segments.name: Andhra Pradesh & Telangana cluster
segments.commentary: Revenue +30% YoY with ARPP IP up 13%; EBITDA more than doubled (+113%) and margin rose over 700 bps to 18.3%.

segments.name: Core hospitals and clinics
segments.commentary: EBITDA +32% YoY, margin 23.1%; excl. Kasargod EBITDA +36%, margin 24.3% (+345 bps).

segments.name: Labs
segments.commentary: External business grew 32% in FY26; Q4 EBITDA +181% YoY, margin 14.7% vs 6.2% a year ago.

segments.name: MVT (medical value travel)
segments.commentary: Revenue +41% YoY on international patient footfall; UAE and Oman softness offset by Maldives and African markets.

guidance_outlook: Management expects the NCLT order for the QCIL merger in May and completion within the quarter; majority of the next period expected under the merged entity.
Management expects no margin dilution from greenfield additions and expects year-on-year margin expansion; Trivandrum brownfield to open around October 2026 (H2 FY27).
Management expects Karnataka IP growth to return to mid-to-high single digits within one to two quarters.
Plans to add ~2,500 beds over 4 years at INR 2,700 crore (INR 350 crore spent to March 2026), taking capacity to over 8,150 beds; Aster's CONGO mix target 60% and then 65%.
capex_capacity: Aster added 290 beds in FY26, taking capacity to 5,449 beds across 20 hospitals including Kasargod.
Launched 159 beds at Aster Whitefield Block D (women and childcare) and 75 beds at Ramesh Ongole in April 2026.
Brownfield pipeline includes 150 beds at MIMS Calicut and 130 beds at MIMS Kannur; Kasargod remains in ramp-up with losses of about INR 19-20 crore in FY26.

Management quoted Aster brownfield and greenfield per-bed cost of roughly INR 0.8-1.1 crore and INR 1.5-1.6 crore respectively in the QCIL answer; QCIL plans ~1,700 beds for ~INR 2,000 crore over 3-4 years, with ~1,500 brownfield.
Combined capacity 10,620+ beds across 28 cities; pipeline of 4,445 beds takes total beyond 15,000.
demand_pricing: Q4 IP volumes up about 7% excluding K&M de-empanelment effect; OP volumes grew double digits.
Cardiology revenue +25% YoY (15% of mix); oncology +23% (11% of mix).
Kerala nurses' strike (from mid-March) settled 13 April 2026; increment cost INR 5-6 crore for ~4,300 nurses.
Competition intense in north Bangalore; attrition of one or two teams in Q3 reversed in Q4.
Aster Whitefield occupancy ~60% for Blocks A-C; Aster CMI 56-60%+; Aster RV 66-69%.

qa_highlights.question: Is Aster or QCIL onboarded to the common insurance empanelment platform, and is it a threat to private chains?
qa_highlights.answer: Varun Khanna said neither QCIL nor Aster has signed up as far as he knows, data privacy and transparency are unresolved, and the framework is not coercive.

qa_highlights.question: Kerala MVT outlook amid Middle East disruption and nurses' issue?
qa_highlights.answer: Ramesh Kumar said UAE and Oman inflows have slowed while Maldives and Africa are rising; the nurses' strike was settled on 13 April with increments of INR 3,250-4,000 per nurse, per T J Wilson.

qa_highlights.question: Drivers of Karnataka IP slowdown to 3% and Aster Aadhar de-empanelment?
qa_highlights.answer: Sunil Kumar said exit from low-yield government schemes (ARPOB under 50% of cash) and competition in north Bangalore caused it; Aster Aadhar runs at 75% occupancy; management sees it as one-off.

qa_highlights.question: Scope to raise CONGO mix and drivers of doctor acquisition?
qa_highlights.answer: Alisha Moopen said CONGO mix is 55% and can go to 60% then 65%; Sunil Kumar cited 36+ new doctors added in six months, excluding replacements.

qa_highlights.question: Per-bed capex for QCIL expansion and Aster margin impact from greenfield?
qa_highlights.answer: Varun Khanna gave QCIL per-bed capex of roughly INR 1-1.1 crore blended, greenfield INR 1.5-1.6 crore, brownfield INR 0.8-1.1 crore. Sunil Kumar said Kasargod cost about 60 bps of margin and no dilution is expected.

qa_highlights.question: Why did QCIL reported EBITDA margin differ from the annual report?
qa_highlights.answer: Sunil Kumar attributed the gap to one-time merger costs and consultant-led productivity work, and said a breakup could be shared later.

risks_watch: NCLT approval timing for the QCIL merger and resulting synergy realisation.
MVT exposure to Middle East (UAE, Oman) softness; shift to Maldives and Africa.
Karnataka IP recovery to mid-to-high single digits after doctor attrition and competition in north Bangalore.
Kasargod ramp-up losses (about INR 19-20 crore in FY26) and Kerala labour cost increments.
Possible industry move to common insurance empanelment, which management says is not yet adopted by large chains.
Reconciliation of ROCE and QCIL EBITDA margin differences versus annual reports.
summary.management_tone: Confident and promotional on growth, margins and expansion, with the merger described as near completion. Management was candid and specific on the Karnataka IP slowdown and attributed it to deliberate exits and competition. Answers on QCIL margin and ROCE definitions were less granular and deferred some detail offline.
key_quotes: Operating EBITDA for the quarter stood at INR 244 crores, growing 26% year-on-year, with margins at 20.7% despite the addition of new capacity.
Based on current timelines, we expect the process to be completed within this quarter.
So, whatever you see is that the 3% is just a one-off thing, it's not a structural issue.

growth.why: Management guides to YoY margin expansion in FY27 with no dilution from greenfields and plans ~2,500 beds over 4 years (INR 2,700 crore, INR 350 crore spent) plus 159 and 75 beds launched in April 2026; Q4 revenue +18% and EBITDA +26% with IP volumes up ~7% ex-K&M, but no explicit revenue growth percentage guided and the bed pipeline runs beyond the 4-quarter window.
